title.en: Tobit Buries the Dead in Nineveh and Loses His Sight
title.zh: 多比在尼尼微葬死者而失明

texts.period: Composed c. 3rd-2nd c. BCE (Aramaic/Hebrew original); principal text: Codex Sinaiticus Greek, 4th c. CE

summary.en: Tobit of the Naphtali exile keeps tithes and alms in Assyria alone among his kinsmen; he carries the dead bodies of murdered Israelites at risk of his life, and his neighbours mock him: 'he is afraid to be killed for the works he does'. Sleeping in his courtyard, sparrow droppings fall in his eyes and he is blind; his wife Anna works for wages, and his rebuke — 'were it not better for us to have alms and righteousness?' — closes the first movement of the book of mercy.
summary.zh: 拿弗他利支派被擄的多比在亞述獨行什一與賙濟；他不顧性命攜葬被殺的以色列人，鄰舍譏笑：「他怕人殺他，但這樣行有何益處？」在院中睡臥，雀糞落入眼中而失明；妻子亞拿做傭工，他的責備——「不如行賙濟行公義」——結束這部憐憫之書的第一幕。

sensitivity.note: Deuterocanonical scripture (scripture for Catholic/Orthodox communities; 'reading' for Jewish tradition); quoted from public-domain KJV Apocrypha. Found in the Cairo Genizah and Qumran in Aramaic and Hebrew.

passages.text: In the days of Shalmaneser king of the Assyrians, I, Tobit, was carried away captive... And because I was mindful of God with all my heart, all the days of my life did I walk righteously... I carried the dead bodies of them into my house; and at midnight I buried them. ... And because I had kept the commandments of God my father, they murmured against me.
passages.note: Verbatim: KJV Apocrypha, Tobit 1:3-19 (public domain), condensed.

passages.text: Resting in the courtyard, warm sparrows fell on his open eyes and left white films; 'whereby I was deprived of my sight'. His wife brought wages, and also a kid; Tobit heard it bleat and said: 'Take heed lest it be stolen; carry it back again'. His wife answered: 'Were it not better for us to have alms and righteousness? For I have brought them, and heard the bleating of the goat.' Tobit was grieved and prayed. Paraphrase of Tobit 2:1-14 (KJV Apocrypha); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Tobit 2:1-14 (KJV Apocrypha); not verbatim.

title.en: Raphael Travels with Tobias: The Demon Asmodeus and the Fish
title.zh: 拉斐爾同行多比雅：惡魔阿斯莫德與魚

region.zh: 往瑪代伊克巴他拿之路

texts.period: Composed c. 3rd-2nd c. BCE; principal text: Codex Sinaiticus Greek, 4th c. CE

summary.en: Sent to Media to reclaim money, young Tobias travels with a 'companion' who is the angel Raphael in disguise. A fish leaps out of the Tigris; the angel orders its heart and liver burned on coals — the smoke drives away the demon Asmodeus, who has killed seven bridegrooms of Sarah; its gall cures Tobit's blind eyes. Raphael reveals himself only at the end: 'I am Raphael, one of the seven holy angels', and teaches: 'alms do deliver from death'.
summary.zh: 多比雅受遣往瑪代取銀，得「同伴」同行——實為喬裝的天使拉斐爾。底格里斯河中大魚躍出；天使命以其心肝於炭上焚燒——烟氣驅走阿斯莫德惡魔，它曾連殺撒拉七個丈夫；魚膽醫好多比的眼睛。末了拉斐爾自顯：「我是拉斐爾，七位聖天使之一」，並教導：「賙濟能救人脫離死亡」。

sensitivity.note: Deuterocanonical scripture; quoted from public-domain KJV Apocrypha. Angelology here (seven holy angels) shaped later Jewish and Christian angel-lore.

passages.text: And they went forth, and came to the river Tigris, and lodged together. And when the young man went down to wash himself, a fish leaped out of the river, and would have devoured him. Then the angel said unto him: 'Take the fish.' And the young man laid hold of the fish, and drew it upon land. ... Then the angel said to him: 'Take the heart and the liver of the fish and put them in thy vessel'; ... And the angel said unto him: 'If thou wilt take this... and make smoke thereof before a man or woman afflicted with any evil spirit, it will drive it away.'
passages.note: Verbatim: KJV Apocrypha, Tobit 6:1-8 (public domain), condensed.

passages.text: Sarah, daughter of Raguel, had been given seven husbands, 'which Asmodeus the evil spirit had killed, before they had lain with her'; the maids blamed her as though she had strangled them. Tobias accepts her in marriage per the law of Moses; the fish-heart and liver are burned on the coals of perfumes, 'the smell thereof put the evil spirit to flight', and the angel pursues him into Egypt and binds him. Tobit's eyes are cured with the gall. Raphael reveals himself: 'I am Raphael, one of the seven holy angels... and all the days of my life did walk with the blind'; and the book closes with the teaching 'it is better to have alms with righteousness than goods without righteousness'. Paraphrase of Tobit 7-8; 11; 12-13 (KJV Apocrypha); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Tobit 7-8; 11-13 (KJV Apocrypha); not verbatim.

title.en: Judith Rebukes the Elders of Bethulia
title.zh: 猶滴斥責比突里亞長老

region.zh: 比突里亞，猶大山地小城

texts.period: Composed c. 2nd-1st c. BCE; principal text: Vulgate/Greek; English: KJV Apocrypha, 1611

summary.en: Holofernes has cut off the city's water; the thirsty people beg Ozias to surrender in five days. Judith — a widow who has lived years in sackcloth and fasting — rebukes him: 'Who are ye, that have tempted God this day?... ye cannot find the depth of the heart of man, neither can ye perceive the things that God will do.' Her five days becomes her own plan: 'what thing soever it be that shall please you, I will do it before the day', and she prays with sackcloth and ashes for strength.
summary.zh: 何樂弗尼截斷城的水源；乾渴的百姓求烏西雅五日內投降。寡婦猶滴——多年披麻禁食——斥責他：「你們今日竟試探神麼？……你們不能參透人心，也不知道神將行何事。」她的五日改為自己的計劃：「你們所喜悅的，我在那日之先必為你們成就」，遂披麻蒙灰祈求力量。

sensitivity.note: Deuterocanonical scripture; quoted from public-domain KJV Apocrypha.

passages.text: And she said to Ozias: 'Who art thou, that hast tempted God this day, and hast stood instead of God among the children of men? And now ye try the Lord God of all fathers... And ye cannot find the bottom of the heart of man, neither can ye perceive the things that he hath prepared. ... For they that are most favored by him shall stand instead of him in doing these things.'
passages.note: Verbatim: KJV Apocrypha, Judith 8:12-16 (public domain), condensed.

title.en: Judith in the Tent of Holofernes
title.zh: 猶滴在何樂弗尼的帳中

region.zh: 比突里亞山下亞述營地

texts.period: Composed c. 2nd-1st c. BCE; principal text: Vulgate/Greek; English: KJV Apocrypha, 1611

summary.en: Judith takes off her widow's sackcloth, bathes, puts on 'her garment of gladness', and walks out with her maid to the enemy camp, praying: 'O God of my father Simeon... make haste and come to mine help'. Holofernes gives her three days' leave to pray; she eats her own provisions. On the fourth night, alone with the drunken general, she prays 'give me strength this day, O Lord God of Israel', takes the sword at his bed's head and strikes his neck twice, rolls off the canopy, and gives the head to her maid.
summary.zh: 猶滴脫下寡婦麻衣，沐浴，穿上「喜樂的衣服」，攜婢走出至敵營，禱告：「我祖西緬的神啊……求你速速來幫助我」。何樂弗尼許她三日祈禱之假；她自帶食物。第四夜，與醉酒的元帥獨處，她求「耶和華以色列的神啊，今日賜我力量」，取帳柱頭上的刀，兩擊其頸，扯下錦帳，將首級交給婢女。

sensitivity.note: Deuterocanonical scripture; quoted from public-domain KJV Apocrypha.

passages.text: And she came to the pillar of the bed, which was at Holofernes' head, and took down the faulchion from it; and approached to his bed, and took hold of the hair of his head; and said: 'Strengthen me, O Lord God of Israel, this day!' And she smote twice upon his neck with all her might, and she took away his head from him. And tumbled down the body from the bed, and pulled down the canopy from the pillars; and anon after she went forth, and gave Holofernes his head to her maid.
passages.note: Verbatim: KJV Apocrypha, Judith 13:6-10 (public domain).

title.en: Judith's Song: The Victory of the Lowly
title.zh: 猶滴之歌：卑微者的得勝

texts.period: Composed c. 2nd-1st c. BCE; principal text: Vulgate/Greek; English: KJV Apocrypha, 1611

summary.en: The head hung on the wall; at dawn the Assyrians flee 'in a valley so strait that they could hardly get out'. Judith's victory-song retells Simeon's sword at Shechem and Jael's tent-pin: 'The Lord hath taken counsel by a woman against our enemies... her beauty deceived him'. The people worship in Jerusalem; she lives to a hundred and five, 'and none did molest her'.
summary.zh: 首級懸於城牆；黎明亞述人在「難以脫出的狹谷」潰逃。猶滴的得勝之歌追述西緬在示劍的刀與雅億的帳橛：「耶和華藉一個女人設謀攻擊我們的仇敵……她的美色迷惑了他」。百姓在耶路撒冷敬拜；她活到一百零五歲，「沒有人擾害她」。

sensitivity.note: Deuterocanonical scripture; quoted from public-domain KJV Apocrypha.

passages.text: Judith said: 'Begin unto my God with timbrels, sing unto my Lord with cymbals, tune unto him a new psalm: exalt him, and call upon his name. For God breaketh the battles: for among the camps in the midst of the people he hath made me conqueror. For the mighty one of Assyria... came from the mountains of the north... and behold, he is broken by a woman's hand.'
passages.note: Verbatim: KJV Apocrypha, Judith 16:1-4 (public domain), condensed.

title.en: Mattathias at Modin: The Revolt Begins
title.zh: 瑪他提亞在摩丁：起義開始

texts.period: Narrative set 167 BCE; composed c. late 2nd-early 1st c. BCE; principal text: Codex Vaticanus Greek; English: KJV Apocrypha, 1611

summary.en: The king's officers demand sacrifice to the idols at Modin. Mattathias, priest of the sons of Joarib, answers before the whole city: 'Though all the nations that are under the king's dominion obey him... yet will I and my sons walk in the covenant of our fathers.' A willing apostate steps to the altar; Mattathias kills him and the king's officer in a fury, then pulls down the altar — and flees to the mountains with his sons, rallying 'every one that is zealous of the law'.
summary.zh: 王的官吏命摩丁眾人向偶像獻祭。約亞里家的祭司瑪他提亞當眾回答：「王的轄下各國雖都聽從他……但我與我兒必照我們列祖的約而行。」一個甘願變節者上前祭壇；瑪他提亞憤而誅之，連同王的官吏一併殺死，拆毀祭壇——攜眾子逃入山地，召集「凡熱心律法者」。

sensitivity.note: Deuterocanonical scripture; quoted from public-domain KJV Apocrypha. Foundational narrative of Hanukkah.

passages.text: Then Mattathias answered and spake with a loud voice: 'Though all the nations that are under the king's dominion obey him, every one having left the religion of his fathers, and given consent to his commandments; yet will I and my sons and my brethren walk in the covenant of our fathers. God forbid that we should forsake the law and the ordinances. We will not hearken to the king's words, to go from our religion, either on the right hand, or the left.'
passages.note: Verbatim: KJV Apocrypha, 1 Maccabees 2:19-22 (public domain).

title.en: Judas Maccabeus: 'For the Battle Is Not to the Multitude'
title.zh: 猶大馬加比：「爭戰的勝敗不全靠人多」

region.zh: 以馬忤斯與伯和崙山道，猶大

texts.period: Narrative set 166-160 BCE; composed c. late 2nd-early 1st c. BCE; principal text: Codex Vaticanus Greek; English: KJV Apocrypha, 1611

summary.en: Judas 'surnamed Maccabeus', 'like as a giant', gathers the faithful; his war-speech enters scripture: 'For the battle is not to the multitude, but success is from heaven... we shall fight for our lives and our laws'. Victory at Beth-horon, Emmaus, and over Nicanor — whose head and hand are displayed at Jerusalem; 'the nations should know that there is one that fighteth for Israel'.
summary.zh: 號稱「馬加比」的猶大「如同巨獅」，召集忠民；其戰前宣言成為經文：「爭戰的勝敗不全靠人多，天上來的能力使人得勝……我們要為性命與律法爭戰」。伯和崙、以馬忤斯、尼迦拿之戰連連得勝——其首與手示於耶路撒冷；「萬國當知道，有一位為以色列爭戰者」。

sensitivity.note: Deuterocanonical scripture; quoted from public-domain KJV Apocrypha.

passages.text: Then answered Judas and said: 'It is no great matter for many that are forbidden to fight to be overcome of a few; for there is no difference in the saving of many or of a few by heaven: for the victory of battle standeth not by the multitude of an host; but strength is from heaven.'
passages.note: Verbatim: KJV Apocrypha, 1 Maccabees 3:17-19 (public domain).

title.en: The Abomination upon the Altar: Antiochus's Persecution
title.zh: 祭壇上的可憎之物：安提阿古之迫害

texts.period: Narrative set 167 BCE; composed c. late 2nd-early 1st c. BCE; principal text: Codex Vaticanus Greek; English: KJV Apocrypha, 1611

summary.en: Antiochus Epiphanes plunders the Temple and issues the decree 'that all should be one people': circumcision forbidden, sabbaths profaned, books of the law burned with those found keeping them put to death. 'The abomination of desolation' is built upon the altar of burnt-offering; women who circumcise their children are cast from the rocks with their babes. 'And there was exceeding great wrath upon Israel.'
summary.zh: 安提阿古四世洗劫聖殿，頒令「使萬民成為一體」：禁割禮、污穢安息日、燒毀律法書，藏書者與守誡者處死。「那行毀壞可憎的」被立於燔祭壇上；為嬰孩行割禮的婦人連嬰孩一同被推下山岩。「以色列中大發烈怒。」

sensitivity.note: Deuterocanonical scripture; quoted from public-domain KJV Apocrypha.

passages.text: And king Antiochus wrote to his whole kingdom, that all should be one people, and every one should leave his laws. ... And they sacrificed to idols the sacrifices forbidden upon the altars. ... And whosoever was found with any the book of the testament, or if any committed himself to it, if he would it according to the law, the king's commandment was, that they should put him to death.
passages.note: Verbatim: KJV Apocrypha, 1 Maccabees 1:41, 54, 57 (public domain), condensed with ellipsis.

title.en: The Mother and Her Seven Sons

texts.period: Composed c. 2nd-1st c. BCE; principal text: Greek; English: KJV Apocrypha, 1611

summary.en: Seven brothers, racked with wheels and scourges, refuse the king's swine's flesh one by one, each answering with resurrection-faith: 'The King of the world shall raise us up, who have died for his laws'. The youngest promises the king: 'We suffer because of our sins... thou shalt find of our nation no more strength'; he is king of the children by outstretched hands. The mother watches all seven die — 'the mother was marvellous above all' — and dies last.
summary.zh: 七兄弟被輪盤拷打，逐一拒食王賜的豬肉，各以復活之信回答：「為他的律法而死的，世界之主要使我們復活」。最小的對王說：「我們受苦是因我們的罪……我民的勇力必不復存」；他向王伸出手臂。母親看著七子逐一死去——「那母親是超乎一切所當讚美的」——最後殉難。

sensitivity.note: Deuterocanonical scripture; quoted from public-domain KJV Apocrypha. Foundational martyrdom narrative read in Jewish as well as Christian tradition (cf. Lamentations Rabbah's Esther-echo).

passages.text: And when he was at the last breath, he said: 'Thou like a fury executors this cruelty without us; but, o thou king, I will not die, for the Lord God raiseth up again his faithful servants unto life again.' ... And after him was the sixth son brought forth, who, when he was a-hanging... said boldly: 'For our own sins, and the sins of our fathers, we receive these things.'
passages.note: Verbatim: KJV Apocrypha, 2 Maccabees 7:9; 7:16 (public domain), condensed with ellipsis.

passages.text: The mother encouraged each son 'with the language of their fathers' reason': 'I was a pure maid, and went not astray, nor nourished up... seven sons born of one mother, all seven died the same day'. Her last speech: 'The Creator of the world... will again have mercy upon them, as he did in the beginning; therefore, now, o thou wretched man, when thou hast already judged thyself worthy of so many plagues, let me alone and my seven sons.' Paraphrase of 2 Maccabees 7:23-41 (KJV Apocrypha); not verbatim.
passages.note: Paraphrase of 2 Maccabees 7:23-41 (KJV Apocrypha); not verbatim.

title.en: Heliodorus Cast Down in the Temple
title.zh: 希利多羅被推倒於聖殿

texts.period: Composed c. 2nd-1st c. BCE; principal text: Greek; English: KJV Apocrypha, 1611

summary.en: Seleucus's minister Heliodorus comes to seize the treasury of widows and orphans kept in the Temple 'for the saying of Heliodorus... that whosoever saw would be filled with wonder at the power of God'. The high priest Onias prays: 'Behold... our sanctuary... is coming to destruction'; while Heliodorus is entering, there appears 'a horse with a terrible rider upon him... having garments of gold' who strikes him — and two young men of 'exceeding beauty', scourging him continuously, cast him down senseless. He is restored only through Onias's sacrifice and testifies: 'there is a certain power of God.'
summary.zh: 西流基的宰相希利多羅奉命奪取聖殿中寡婦孤兒的存款，因「他看見的必因神的大能滿心驚訝」之語。大祭司阿尼亞禱告：「看哪……我們的聖所……將被毀壞」；他進入之際，有「一匹可怕的馬，上面有騎者，披著金甲」擊打他——並有「極其俊美的二位少年」不斷鞭打他，使之昏迷倒地。惟藉阿尼亞的祭得以痊癒，且見證：「確有神的權能。」

sensitivity.note: Deuterocanonical scripture; quoted from public-domain KJV Apocrypha.

passages.text: But when they were now at the treasury of the temple, and he that kept the door was come in, there was suddenly... a great horse with a terrible rider upon him, in rich array, and he rushed fiercely, striking Heliodorus with his fore-feet. And he that sat upon him seemed to have armour of gold, and his raiment was like to that of a man running swiftly for a prize.
passages.note: Verbatim: KJV Apocrypha, 2 Maccabees 3:25-26 (public domain).

title.en: Nicanor Falls: The Day Before the Day of Mordecai
title.zh: 尼迦拿傾覆：末底改日的前一日

texts.period: Narrative set 161 BCE; composed c. 2nd-1st c. BCE; principal text: Greek; English: KJV Apocrypha, 1611

summary.en: Before the battle with Nicanor, Judas encourages his men with a dream: the dead high priest Onias and the prophet Jeremiah appear — 'Jeremiah stretched forth his right hand and gave unto Judas a golden sword, saying: Take this holy sword, a gift from God'. Nicanor falls; his head and right hand are cut off and displayed at Jerusalem; the day before Purim is kept as Nicanor's Day.
summary.zh: 與尼迦拿交戰之前，猶大以異夢激勵軍士：亡故的大祭司阿尼亞與先知耶利米顯現——「耶利米伸出右手，賜給猶大一柄金劍，說：拿這聖劍，這是神的恩賜」。尼迦拿倒下；其首與右手被割，示於耶路撒冷；普珥日之前一日定為尼迦拿日。

sensitivity.note: Deuterocanonical scripture; quoted from public-domain KJV Apocrypha.

passages.text: Then Onias the high priest lifting up his hands, prayed for the whole body of the Jews, saying in this manner: 'O Lord God... this holy city, and the temple of thine heritage... and Jeremiah the prophet, who is the writer of the resurrection to them that believe, gave his right hand and gave Judas a sword of gold, and said unto him: Take this holy sword, a gift from God, wherewith thou shalt wound the adversaries.'
passages.note: Verbatim: KJV Apocrypha, 2 Maccabees 15:12-16 (public domain), condensed.

title.en: Let Us Now Praise Famous Men: Ben Sira 44
title.zh: 我們當讚美顯揚之人：便西拉四十四章

region.zh: 耶路撒冷，文士學堂（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Composed c. 190-175 BCE (Hebrew original, translated into Greek c. 132 BCE by grandson); principal text: Cairo Genizah Hebrew MS

summary.en: Ben Sira's hymn to the ancestors: 'Let us now praise famous men, and our fathers that begat us... such as have left a name behind them'. Abraham 'the great father of a multitude of nations', Moses 'beloved of God and men', and on through the judges and prophets — the memory of the tradition kept alive by the scribe's own office: 'the assembly shall show forth their wisdom'.
summary.zh: 便西拉對先祖的頌歌：「我們當讚美顯揚之人，及生育我們的列祖……這些人留下名聲」。亞伯拉罕「萬國的大父」，摩西「神與世人所愛」，繼而士師與先知——由文士的職分保存記憶：「會眾必述他們的智慧。」

sensitivity.note: Deuterocanonical wisdom book; quoted from public-domain KJV Apocrypha. Hebrew text recovered from the Cairo Genizah (1896).

passages.text: Let us now praise famous men, and our fathers that begat us. The Lord hath wrought great glory by them through his great power from the beginning. Such as did bear rule in their kingdoms, men renowned for their power, giving counsel by their understanding... These were merciful men, whose righteousness hath not been forgotten. With their seed shall continually remain a good inheritance, and their children are within the covenant.
passages.note: Verbatim: KJV Apocrypha, Ecclesiasticus 44:1-12 (public domain), condensed.

title.en: Wisdom Praise Her Own Work: Ben Sira 24
title.zh: 智慧頌己工：便西拉二十四章

region.zh: 耶路撒冷，聖殿院宇（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Composed c. 190-175 BCE; principal text: Cairo Genizah Hebrew MS; English: KJV Apocrypha, 1611

summary.en: Ben Sira's Wisdom-hymn, Jewish counterpart to Proverbs 8 and forerunner of John's Logos: 'I came out of the mouth of the Most High... Before the mountains... I was brought forth'. Wisdom seeks a resting place through the whole earth and is commanded: 'Make thy dwelling in Jacob' — she flourishes as the law 'which Moses commanded us', a river of understanding pouring forth teaching like prophecy.
summary.zh: 便西拉的智慧頌，箴言八章的猶太呼應，約翰邏各斯之源：「我出於至高者之口……在山嶺之先，我被生出」。智慧遍尋安身之地，得命：「在雅各中住下」——作為「摩西所吩咐我們的律法」而榮耀，如理解之河，教導湧流如預言。

sensitivity.note: Deuterocanonical wisdom book; quoted from public-domain KJV Apocrypha.

passages.text: I came out of the mouth of the Most High, and covered the earth as a cloud. I dwelt in high places, and my throne is in a cloudy pillar. I alone compassed the circuit of heaven, and walked in the bottom of the deep. ... In every nation and people I was. With all these I sought rest; and in whose inheritance shall I abide? So the Creator of all things gave me a commandment, and he that made me caused my tabernacle to rest, and said: 'Lodge in Jacob, and in Israel take thine inheritance.'
passages.note: Verbatim: KJV Apocrypha, Ecclesiasticus 24:3-8 (public domain), condensed.

title.en: Prayer for the Exiles: Baruch's Confession
title.zh: 為被擄者的祈禱：巴錄的認罪

texts.period: Composed c. 2nd-1st c. BCE (attributed to Jeremiah's scribe); principal text: Greek; English: KJV Apocrypha, 1611

summary.en: Baruch, 'the son of Nerias', reads the words of the book in Babylon, gathering silver for offerings to Jerusalem's sanctuary; the confession follows: 'Unto the Lord our God belongeth righteousness, but unto us confusion of faces'. The famous invitation: 'Learn where is wisdom, where is strength, where is understanding... who hath gone up into heaven, and taken her?... but he that knoweth all things knoweth her; he found her by his own count.'
summary.zh: 尼利亞的兒子巴錄在巴比倫宣讀書中言語，收集銀子為聖殿獻祭；認罪隨後：「公義屬耶和華我們的神，至於我們，當羞愧滿面」。著名的邀請：「智慧在哪裡？能力在哪裡？聰明在哪裡……誰曾上天取下她？……惟知道一切事的神認識她；他以自己的計謀尋見她。」

sensitivity.note: Deuterocanonical scripture; quoted from public-domain KJV Apocrypha.

passages.text: And now, Lord Almighty, God of Israel, the grieving soul in great trouble crieth: 'Hear, O Lord, and have mercy; for we are sinners before thee. Thou art set forth for ever, and we perish for ever.' O Lord Almighty, thou God of Israel, hear now the prayers of the dead Israelites, and of their children, which have sinned before thee, and not hearkened unto the voice of thee their God.
passages.note: Verbatim: KJV Apocrypha, Baruch 3:2-5 (public domain).

title.en: Daniel Serves Bel and Slays the Dragon
title.zh: 但以理事奉彼勒並殺龍

texts.period: Composed c. 3rd-2nd c. BCE (Greek addition to Daniel); principal text: LXX/Theodotion; English: KJV Apocrypha, 1611

source.work: Bel and the Dragon (English: KJV Apocrypha, 1611)

summary.en: The king asks Daniel why he worships not Bel; Daniel answers: 'because I do not worship idols made with hands, but the living God'. A night-watch exposes the seventy priests consuming the offerings secretly; the ashes test proves the fraud, and the priests are cast in. Then the dragon — 'a great dragon, and the Babylonians worshipped him' — is killed by Daniel's recipe of pitch, fat, and hair: 'and they that drank of it died', and the dragon bursts.
summary.zh: 王問但以理為何不拜彼勒；他答：「我不拜手所造的偶像，但拜永活的神」。夜間守候揭露七十祭司暗食祭物；灰燼之試證其詐，祭司被投入。繼而那龍——「巴比倫人所拜的大龍」——被但以理的配方（瀝青、脂、髮）所殺：「喫的都死了」，龍即爆裂。

sensitivity.note: Deuterocanonical (Greek additions to Daniel); quoted from public-domain KJV Apocrypha.

passages.text: Then Daniel took pitch, and fat, and hair, and did seethe them together, and made lumps thereof: this he gave in manner unto the dragon to eat; and the dragon did eat it, and burst in sunder. And he said: 'Lo, these are the gods ye worship, and they that eat of them shall die.'
passages.note: Verbatim: KJV Apocrypha, Bel and the Dragon, v. 27 (public domain).

texts.period: Composed c. 3rd-2nd c. BCE (Greek addition to Daniel); principal text: LXX/Theodotion; English: KJV Apocrypha, 1611

summary.en: The beautiful wife of Joacim is ambushed by two judges in her husband's garden; refusing them, she is falsely accused of adultery and condemned by her own beauty as evidence. Young Daniel, moved by the Spirit, cross-examines the elders apart from each other — 'under what tree sawest thou them together?' — mallow and evergreen oak; the answers differ, and the judges are executed by the law they misused. 'And there arose such a cry and shout... for Susanna'; 'from that day forth was Daniel had in reputation.'
summary.zh: 約雅金的美好妻子在園中被二審判官伏擊；拒絕後被誣告通姦，其美貌竟成罪證。少年但以理受靈感動，隔開二長老分別訊問——「你們在什麼樹下見他們行淫？」——乳香樹與長青橡樹；答案相異，濫用律法的審判官反被所立之法處死。「全會眾呼喊大聲……為蘇撒拿」；「從那日起，但以理在眾民眼前大得尊榮。」

sensitivity.note: Deuterocanonical (Greek additions to Daniel); quoted from public-domain KJV Apocrypha. Read in the Easter Vigil of the Western tradition; noted for its legal drama.

passages.text: Then Daniel stood up in the midst of them, and said: 'Are ye so foolish, O ye sons of Israel, that without examination or knowledge of the truth ye have condemned a daughter of Israel?' ... So he put them asunder one from another, and called one of them, and said unto him: 'O thou that art grown old in evil days, now are thy sins come to purpose, which thou hast committed beforetime... Under what tree sawest thou them companying together?'
passages.note: Verbatim: KJV Apocrypha, Susanna, vv. 48-53 (public domain), condensed.

title.en: The Three Bodyguards and Zerubbabel's Answer
title.zh: 三侍衛與所羅巴伯之答

region.zh: 波斯王庭（以書珊象徵性定位）

texts.period: Composed c. 2nd-1st c. BCE (Greek expansion of Ezra material); principal text: LXX; English: KJV Apocrypha, 1611

summary.en: Darius's three bodyguards compete: what is strongest — wine, the king, or women? Zerubbabel's answer wins the prize and the king's promise: 'Truth is the greatest of all... it endureth and shall continue for ever, and liveth and conquereth for evermore'. His reward — the rebuilding of Jerusalem and the return of the sacred vessels — he asks for his father's city.
summary.zh: 大流士的三侍衛比試：何者最強——酒、王、或女人？所羅巴伯之答得賞與王許：「真理最大……它堅立，必永存，並永遠得勝而活」。所求的賞賜——重建耶路撒冷與聖器歸還——他為祖城求之。

sensitivity.note: Deuterocanonical scripture; quoted from public-domain KJV Apocrypha.

passages.text: Then answered Zorobabel: 'O king, wine is not the strongest, nor the king; nor are women, though they bear the mastery of men; nor yet are these things that ye have said; but truth passeth all these things, and shall overcome them. For, O king, all things obey truth; and the earth obeyeth truth... Truth endureth, and is always strong; it liveth and conquereth for evermore, without respecting of persons in judging.',
passages.note: Verbatim: KJV Apocrypha, 1 Esdras 4:34-38 (public domain).
